info.title: Archy Agents API
info.description:
AgentScope-based multi-tenant RAG + multi-agent orchestration API.

Authentication uses a bearer JWT that includes `org_id` and `project_id`. Most endpoints are explicitly scoped by those IDs in the path and will return 403 if the token tenant does not match.

post.summary: Create documents from a local folder
post.description:
Use case: ingest all supported files from a local folder into a knowledge base.

Partial success: returns both created documents and per-file errors.
Deduplication: unchanged files (same name, size, mtime) are skipped.

Indexing is automatically enqueued for each created document.

Auth: Bearer JWT; `org_id` and `project_id` must match token tenancy.

Use case: ingest Confluence pages into a knowledge base by fetching content and extracting text.

The pages are read with the caller's own Atlassian connection selected by `integration_id` (owner, site and credentials are never accepted from the request). The created source is bound to that connection and owner. No platform credentials are used.

Partial success: returns both created documents and per-page errors.
Change detection: pages with unchanged versions are skipped on re-ingestion.

Indexing is automatically enqueued for each created document.

Auth: user token only; the user must belong to `org_id` and be a member of `project_id`. Errors use `{detail: {code, message}}`.

Use case: import Confluence pages into a knowledge base without waiting. The request is validated and a source bound to the caller's own Atlassian connection is found (same connection and same page URLs reuse one source) or created; the pages are read after the response and progress is stored on the source (`GET .../sources/{source_id}` -> `sync_progress` and `indexing`).

One import runs per source: while it is syncing a repeated request starts nothing and returns the running source with `already_running` true. A source with no progress for 15 minutes is treated as abandoned and restarted.

Same body, owner rules and `{detail: {code, message}}` errors as `documents/from-confluence`, which keeps its blocking behavior.

post.summary: Start a background refresh of a Confluence source
post.description: Use case: refresh a Confluence source without waiting. Only the user who owns the source's Atlassian connection can refresh it; unbound sources return 409 `source_rebind_required`. Progress and duplicate prevention work as for `confluence-imports`: a source that is already syncing starts nothing and returns `already_running` true.

post.description:
Execute a workflow and stream progress via Server-Sent Events (SSE).

**Orchestrator workflows** emit: `start`, `step_started` / `step_completed` per agent, then `end`.

**Other workflow types** emit: `start`, optional `token` / `discussion` events, then `end`.

**Legacy workflow types** (sequential/parallel/routing/dialog/conversation/orchestrator/handoff/debate) additionally interleave the unified trace envelope (`run.started`/`node.started`/`node.delta`/`node.completed`/`edge.active`/`run.completed`), each carrying `seq` so clients can resume with `?after_seq=N`.

**Structured output**: when the workflow has a `structured_output_schema` configured, the final validated object is streamed exactly once as a discrete `structured_output` event (`data.object`), immediately followed by `run.completed` carrying the same object in `data.structured_output`. This is always the complete, schema-validated object — never a partial/incremental JSON fragment. If the object fails schema validation, no `structured_output` event is emitted and `run.completed` carries `data.structured_output_error` instead.

NOTE: event payloads may include additional fields; clients should treat unknown keys as forward-compatible.

On failure, an `error` event replaces `end`.

Pass `after_seq` (query param) together with a `session_id` (body) to resume a dropped stream: persisted trace envelopes with `seq > after_seq` are replayed first, then live streaming continues.

inputs.title: Inputs
inputs.description: Only inputs declared `sensitive` are accepted (they are not stored with the paused run and must be sent again); any other key returns 400. Other inputs are restored.

session_id.title: Session Id

status.title: Status
status.description: pending | running | awaiting_input | succeeded | failed. `awaiting_input`: paused at a checkpoint node; `output` is the prompt and the pending question is in the session `state.pending_input`.

status.title: Status
status.description: Derived from `state.status`: `awaiting_input` (paused at a checkpoint), `failed` (a checkpoint failed, e.g. expired) or `cancelled`. `completed` means only 'no waiting/failed/cancelled marker': it also covers a session that never ran and ordinary run failures, which are not marked. pending_input_summary.description: Only for `awaiting_input`: checkpoint node name and expiry, no question text.
